title: Experimental records and seeds
goals: Record enough detail to reproduce a run
Report all planned seeds instead of selecting the best

prerequisite.prompt: What must accompany a reported validation score?
prerequisite.answer: The model version, split, metric, data provenance and development choices.

vocabulary: An initial value controlling a pseudo-random process
A saved account of inputs, settings and outputs
Ability to repeat a specified procedure
Reporting favorable results while hiding relevant others

blocks.text: A seed can help repeat a random split or initialization, but it is not a magic quality stamp. Save data version, split membership, code version, settings, preprocessing, seed and metric definition. Some software operations remain nondeterministic, so document tolerances and environment too.

Use fictional classroom data throughout this investigation. Keep the task, units, reference labels and data split visible as you reason. Earlier weeks supplied the model-building process; this week examines experimental records and seeds.

A team declares seeds 11, 22, 33 before running. Validation accuracies are 14/20, 16/20, 12/20:70, 80, 60 percent. Mean accuracy is 70 percent, with a 20-percentage-point range. Reporting only seed 22 as the model result hides the declared experiment.

Before continuing, underline the decision rule and circle the evidence that supports the conclusion. Explain the example to a partner without replacing the counts or conditions with a stronger claim. Keep the distinction between an observed result and a proposed next step.

blocks.title: Experimental records and seeds at a glance
blocks.caption: The seed is part of the procedure, not evidence that a split represents the target population. Reproducing leakage perfectly reproduces a mistake. Check group separation and legitimate features before celebrating identical outputs.

blocks.label: A file contains only seed 22 and 80 percent. Name four missing items. Explain the steps or evidence behind your response.

blocks.text: A small record can contain run ID, timestamp, dataset checksum, training and validation IDs, model settings, feature version, seed, predictions and notes. Keep personal information out of exported logs. Save failed runs with reasons instead of quietly removing them.

When comparing two methods, use the same declared splits or seeds where appropriate and compare paired results. A mean across reused samples does not automatically provide a statistical confidence claim. Report the procedure and observed variation plainly.

blocks.label: One planned seed fails before prediction. How should it appear in the record?

workbook.title: Summarize all runs
workbook.prompt: Calculate the worked mean and range in percentage points.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Mean 70 percent; range 80-60=20 percentage points, across the three declared runs.

workbook.title: Improve a record
workbook.prompt: A file contains only seed 22 and 80 percent. Name four missing items.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Examples: data version, split IDs, model settings, code version, metric denominator and full planned-run results.

workbook.title: Separate two ideas
workbook.prompt: Does identical output prove a valid experiment?
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: No. A deterministic experiment can still contain leakage, invalid labels or an unrepresentative split.

workbook.title: Apply independently
workbook.prompt: Declared seeds 1, 2, 3 produce 9/12, 8/12, 10/12 correct. Compute the mean accuracy and range.
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Mean 27/36=75 percent; range(10-8)/12=1/6 about 16.7 percentage points. Retain all three runs.

workbook.title: Handle a failed run
workbook.prompt: One planned seed fails before prediction. How should it appear in the record?
workbook.answer: Teacher explanation: Record the failed run, cause and any retry; disclose which runs contributed to summaries and do not invent its score.

teacher.background: Teach two 45-minute sessions. This week focuses on experimental records and seeds. Model the worked example first, collect the new W 4 case independently before feedback, and use the fresh retry to check transfer. Award credit for traceable reasoning and bounded claims, including justified uncertainty.
materials: Paper, pencils and a calculator for fractions
The fictional examples and a blank evidence table
Saved classroom project records for critique; no personal student dataset required
sessions: Use the prerequisite question: What must accompany a reported validation score? Check the explanation before proceeding.
Read the opening and model the worked evidence. Ask students to identify seed in context.
Complete W 1 and W 2 with support: summarize all runs; improve a record. Require the evidence, not only the final response.
Read the visual row by row. Collect the guided explanation and compare reasoning in pairs. Connect each conclusion to the stated evidence.
Retrieve the distinction between seed and run record. Invite a counterexample to an overconfident claim.
Discuss the application and complete W 3: Does identical output prove a valid experiment?
Collect W4 independently before giving hints. Assess these outcomes: Record enough detail to reproduce a run; Distinguish reproducibility from validity. Record any support used.
Use W 5 and the exit response to assess limits. Give targeted feedback, then the fresh retry. Save evidence of independent understanding.
teacher.guidedAnswer: Guided response: Examples: data version, split IDs, model settings, code version, metric denominator and full planned-run results. Exit response: Record the failed run, cause and any retry; disclose which runs contributed to summaries and do not invent its score.
misconceptions: Ask for the relevant counts, units, procedure or saved record. For this week: Mean 70 percent; range 80-60=20 percentage points, across the three declared runs.
A stronger claim makes a stronger project
Record the failed run, cause and any retry; disclose which runs contributed to summaries and do not invent its score.
The new case can be copied from the example
The independent task changes the evidence. Require a fresh explanation: Mean 27/36=75 percent; range(10-8)/12=1/6 about 16.7 percentage points. Retain all three runs.
teacher.assessment: For independent W 4, require: Mean 27/36=75 percent; range(10-8)/12=1/6 about 16.7 percentage points. Retain all three runs. Fresh retry accuracies 50, 60, 70 percent: mean 60 percent, range 20 percentage points. Require all declared runs and their denominators. Mark each criterion as independent, supported or not yet demonstrated. Reassess the reasoning after feedback; do not replace the first attempt silently.
teacher.support: Provide a blank evidence table and allow a verbal explanation before writing. Highlight the given conditions without supplying the W 4 conclusion. Use seed and run record in full sentences. Extension: alter one condition in the worked example and explain which conclusion changes and which remains supported.
teacher.next: Next week: Distribution shift. Carry forward the saved evidence and the distinction between development choices and justified claims.
